source.title: Explaining Grokking and Information Bottleneck through Neural Collapse Emergence

record.tranche_reason: Tests grokking-like delayed generalization in new, non-algorithmic image and text classification settings and reports how it varies by architecture, initialization, weight decay, and training-set size.
record.gate_note: The study measures training and test accuracy during training, including settings where the authors explicitly report grokking and settings where it does not occur. It explicitly treats modular arithmetic as outside the scope of its classification analysis. Its discussion of circuits and optimizer/numerical artifacts is not tested. The information-bottleneck results do not measure a claim version's named grokking behavior.
record.test_reason: Measures train and test accuracy over training on non-algorithmic image and text classification. It reports a grokking-like delay for MLPs on MNIST and Fashion-MNIST, and no delay for CNN, ViT and text transformers, so it bears directly on V3.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors argue that contraction of population within-class variance, tracked via neural collapse (RNC1) on a slower time scale than fitting, explains both grokking and the information-bottleneck compression phase, and that weight decay speeds it up. Empirically, grokking appears only in the MLP image settings; CNN, ViT and text transformers show none.
record.recipe_differences: Uses image and text classification rather than small algorithmic datasets; the main grokking experiment follows an MNIST classification setup, with an MLP trained using AdamW.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported timing and presence of grokking vary by architecture and setting. Stronger weight decay accelerates grokking in the MLP image experiments; CNN, ViT, and text-transformer experiments report no grokking. Scaling initialization by 8 makes little difference in the text experiments.

fits_no_version.finding: The decrease of within-class representation variance (RNC1) coincides with the test-accuracy jump in MLP grokking, not with training-set fitting, across weight decays.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Grokking on classification coincides with the late contraction of within-class variance (neural collapse), whose time scale grows as weight decay shrinks.

record.problems: The experiments do not test algorithmic datasets. Several figures report averaged results over five seeds but the main text does not provide numerical values for individual weight-decay conditions; the outcomes are mainly qualitative. Grokking is not observed in several tested architectures and text settings.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-relevant training/test-accuracy outcomes were left out. Results about RNC1, NC1, NC2, and information-bottleneck estimates alone were not recorded because they do not measure the grokking behaviors specified by the tested claim version.

untested.parts: Molecules; a standard-vs-large-init or weight-norm comparison in the MLP setting where grokking occurs (MLPs were always run with init ×8); an explicit lazy-to-rich transition.
All parts: modular arithmetic was explicitly excluded from scope.
No critical dataset size or ungrokking; weight decay is varied only for timing.
No comparison of algorithms across runs.

missing.what: CNN fitting-phase vs convergence accuracy: test accuracy 86% at step 2,700 rising to 94% at step 100k after train accuracy hits 100%. This is gradual post-fit improvement, not grokking.
Theorem 4.3 predicts the delay between fitting and the RNC1 time scale grows as about 1/λ for small weight decay (theoretical only).

record.verdict_notes: Not an original source. The MLP setup follows Omnigrok (Liu et al. 2023a) with init ×8, so the large-init condition is built in rather than toggled. The CNN/ViT/text 'absent' results used only partial init scaling for stability, which weakens their bearing on the init-scale switch. IB/MI results (Figures 4, 13, 14) do not measure grokking.

versions.untested_parts: The experiments are on image and text classification, not small algorithmic datasets such as modular arithmetic; the authors explicitly exclude modular arithmetic from scope.
Tracks RNC1 and other representation geometry, but does not identify or track a generalizing circuit, memorizing components, or a circuit-level progress measure anticipating a test-accuracy jump.

Does not test molecules, large realistic models, or a systematic switch between grokking and no grokking caused by initialization scale or weight norm. Weight decay and initialization are varied in some settings.
Varies weight decay and reports timing effects, but does not test the efficiency account, critical dataset size, or ungrokking.
Does not identify or compare algorithms learned across runs.
Does not test adaptive-optimizer instabilities or floating-point limits in the softmax as explanations of grokking.

relationships.condition: 4-layer MLP with init ×8 and AdamW, on MNIST and Fashion-MNIST with 1000 samples
relationships.reason: Train accuracy saturates at 100% while test accuracy stays at 15%, then reaches 88% much later; grokking is replicated on Fashion-MNIST, and stronger weight decay shortens the delay (r1-r5).
relationships.display_finding: Training accuracy reached 100% while test accuracy remained at 15% before later reaching 88%, with grokking also reproduced on Fashion-MNIST and shortened by stronger weight decay.

relation.reason: Directly measures training and test dynamics, including occurrence and absence of delayed generalization relevant to V3.

tranche.reason: Reports grokking results in additional image settings and tests its occurrence across CNN, ViT and text-transformer settings.

source_check.notes: Interpret r1 together with r2 as the temporal evidence for grokking. CNN scaling affects only fully connected layers; ViT scaling affects feedforward layers and the linear head. The supplied study text is the January 2026 v2, published at ICLR 2026.
